# Capitalization

> **这页管什么**：标题用句首大写（sentence case），不用标题式大写。
>
> 来源：<https://developers.google.com/style/capitalization> · CC BY 4.0 · 本文件是**规则摘要**，非原文全文。

## General

- Follow standard American English capitalization.
- Before capitalizing a word, think about why and whether it should be capitalized.
- Don't use capitalization differences to distinguish meaning (capital *Pod* vs lowercase *pod*) — casual readers miss the distinction.
- Avoid all-uppercase text except for official names, standard all-caps abbreviations, or code.
- Avoid camel case except in official names or when referencing code.

## Titles and headings

- **Use sentence case**: capitalize only the first word, the first word in a subheading after a colon, and any proper nouns.
- Don't put a period at the end of a title or heading.
- When referencing a title from a document that follows this guide, use sentence case regardless of the original casing.
- When referencing titles from outside sources, keep original capitalization.

## After colons

Lowercase the first word after a colon, except for proper nouns, headings, quotations, and text following labels like *Caution* or *Note*.

## Figures, glossaries, lists, tables

- Sentence case for captions, labels, callouts, and in-image text.
- Glossary and index terms lowercase unless proper nouns; definitions in sentence case.
- Sentence case for all list items.
- Sentence case for table contents, headings, labels, and captions.

## Hyphenated words

When a hyphenated word starts a sentence or heading, capitalize only the first part, unless a later element is a proper noun.

## Naming casing styles

Avoid naming casing conventions (*camel case*, *snake case*) — they don't localize well and aren't standardized. Describe the requirement directly and give an example.
